The goal is to validate completeness of paging signals and ensure incidents are owned consistently.\\n\\n# Inclusion criteria\\n- Production customer impact\\n- Primary failure mode: capacity exhaustion, quota exhaustion, or provisioning blocked by quota\\n- Occurred between 2025-01-01 and 2025-06-30\\n\\n# Incident list (canonical for H1 2025)\\n| Incident ID | Date | Product surface | Failure mode | Primary owner (team) | Canonical artifact |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| INC-2025-0112 | 2025-01-12 | Hosted API (us-east) | GPU pool capacity exhaustion | Eng Infra | Confluence postmortem: INC-2025-0112 |\\n| INC-2025-0217 | 2025-02-17 | Console/Rollouts | Quota prevented canary capacity add | Eng Platform | Jira INT-489 + Slack thread |\\n| INC-2025-0303 | 2025-03-03 | Dedicated (eu-west) | Provisioning blocked by quota + autoscaler lag | Eng SRE | Confluence postmortem: INC-2025-0303 |\\n| INC-2025-0411 | 2025-04-11 | Hosted API | Misdiagnosed as memory pressure; confirmed quota exhaustion on burst pool | Eng Serving Runtime | Jira INT-556 |\\n| INC-2025-0522 | 2025-05-22 | Private (VPC) | Effective capacity drop via GPU fragmentation | Eng Infra | Confluence postmortem: INC-2025-0522 |\\n\\n# Observations\\n- Two incidents were driven by quota ceilings preventing scale-up (INC-2025-0217, INC-2025-0303).\\n- One incident (INC-2025-0411) was initially triaged as runtime memory pressure but root-caused to quota exhaustion and provisioning failures for the burst pool.\\n\\n# Action items\\n1. document.content:
{
  "title": "Incident Review Summary (H1 2025): Capacity & quota exhaustion incidents  paging and ownership gaps",
  "space": "eng-sre",
  "author": "Grace OConnor",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-06-18",
  "last_updated": "2025-06-28",
  "reviewers": [
    "Ethan Park",
    "Maya Srinivasan",
    "Ava Chen",
    "Rohan Mehta"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "incident-review",
    "capacity",
    "quota",
    "h1-2025",
    "action-items"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "# Purpose
This page summarizes all production incidents in H1 2025 where the dominant failure mode was **GPU capacity exhaustion** or **quota exhaustion** (including cases where quota prevented provisioning). The goal is to validate completeness of paging signals and ensure incidents are owned consistently.

# Inclusion criteria
- Production customer impact
- Primary failure mode: capacity exhaustion, quota exhaustion, or provisioning blocked by quota
- Occurred between 2025-01-01 and 2025-06-30

# Incident list (canonical for H1 2025)
| Incident ID | Date | Product surface | Failure mode | Primary owner (team) | Canonical artifact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| INC-2025-0112 | 2025-01-12 | Hosted API (us-east) | GPU pool capacity exhaustion | Eng Infra | Confluence postmortem: INC-2025-0112 |
| INC-2025-0217 | 2025-02-17 | Console/Rollouts | Quota prevented canary capacity add | Eng Platform | Jira INT-489 + Slack thread |
| INC-2025-0303 | 2025-03-03 | Dedicated (eu-west) | Provisioning blocked by quota + autoscaler lag | Eng SRE | Confluence postmortem: INC-2025-0303 |
| INC-2025-0411 | 2025-04-11 | Hosted API | Misdiagnosed as memory pressure; confirmed quota exhaustion on burst pool | Eng Serving Runtime | Jira INT-556 |
| INC-2025-0522 | 2025-05-22 | Private (VPC) | Effective capacity drop via GPU fragmentation | Eng Infra | Confluence postmortem: INC-2025-0522 |

# Observations
- Two incidents were driven by quota ceilings preventing scale-up (INC-2025-0217, INC-2025-0303).
- One incident (INC-2025-0411) was initially triaged as runtime memory pressure but root-caused to quota exhaustion and provisioning failures for the burst pool.

# Action items
1. Standardize a single label for capacity/quota incidents across Jira + postmortems (owner: Eng SRE)
2. Add a preflight check in rollouts: do not start canary if regional GPU quota headroom < 10% (owner: Eng Platform)
3. Improve runbook guidance for distinguishing memory pressure vs capacity/quota exhaustion (owner: Eng Serving Runtime)

# Links
- INT-517, INT-544, INT-556, INT-601
- Slack: #incidents thread (INC-2025-0217)
",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "body"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_bce6ec1b34a044d694dda5607a184d31"
}

    "title": "Sustained elevated 5xx after regional failover; retry amplification and serving-runtime crashloops",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/jira",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"SUP-87422\",\n  \"project\": \"customer-support\",\n  \"issue_type\": \"Incident\",\n  \"summary\": \"Sustained elevated 5xx after regional failover; retry amplification and serving-runtime crashloops\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"severity\": \"Sev1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"reporter\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marco Bell\",\n  \"customer_company\": \"NoteBase Inc.\",\n  \"customer_tier\": \"dedicated\",\n  \"components\": [\n    \"api-gateway\",\n    \"serving-runtime\",\n    \"autoscaler\",\n    \"kvcache\",\n    \"routing\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"5xx\",\n    \"regional-failover\",\n    \"retry-amplification\",\n    \"high-error-rate\"\n  ],\n  \"environment\": \"prod: us-west -> failover -> eu-west\",\n  \"affected_models\": [\n    \"redwood-v1-medium\"\n  ],\n  \"affected_regions\": [\n    \"us-west-2\",\n    \"eu-west-1\"\n  ],\n  \"sla_due_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"first_response_due_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"linked_issues\": [\n    \"SUP-62111\",\n    \"SUP-44120\"\n  ],\n  \"related_github_prs\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/3482\"\n  ],\n  \"related_confluence_pages\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/FAILOVER-RUNBOOK\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Issue summary: After an automated regional failover on 2026-03-10 at ~03:14 UTC, NoteBase began observing sustained 5xx responses for their production traffic. Impact: customer reports 30-40% of requests returning 5xx (502/503/504) for ~90 minutes and higher latency for the remainder. Environment: NoteBase dedicated tenancy; traffic routed from us-west-2 to eu-west-1 as part of failover policy. Immediate business impact: degraded UX for end users, automated client retries increased request volume.\",\n  \"impact\": \"Customer-facing production errors; estimated 35% elevated 5xx rate for the customer\\u2019s routes; increased cost due to retries and partial throttling by gateway.\",\n  \"steps_to_reproduce\": \"1) Trigger a regional failover by simulating control-plane evicted nodes scenario in us-west-2 (internal test). 2) Observe routing shift to eu-west-1. 3) Under steady client QPS with exponential backoff disabled, observe a ramp of 5xxs within 5-10 minutes as KV cache warms and runtimes restart. 4) Verify serving-runtime logs showing OOM-ish restarts and high GC/CPU prior to 5xx wave.\",\n  \"logs_and_metrics\": \"Summarized metrics: gateway 5xx rate jump at 03:14 UTC; serving-runtime process restarts increased 6x; average p95 latency rose from 180ms to 900ms; worker OOM and eviction logs in runtime. Dashboard links: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/ingress/route-NoteBase?from=164&to=204, runtime crash heatmap: https://dash.redwood.ai/runtime/crashmap?range=2h.\",\n  \"investigation_notes\": [\n    \"03:20 UTC - Initial triage: observed routing diverted to eu-west-1; autoscaler initiated scale-up but aggressive scale-down cooldown was still in place causing unstable pool size.\",\n    \"03:35 UTC - Hypothesis: client retries (no jitter) created retry amplification hitting runtimes before KV cache/memory warmed, causing thrash and restarts leading to 5xxs.\",\n    \"03:50 UTC - Evidence: runtime logs show frequent cache misses and high alloc rates; OOM-like terminations preceded many 5xx events. Stack traces attached in linked PR notes.\",\n    \"04:10 UTC - Correlation: customer client library was configured with immediate retries (3 attempts, no backoff). We reproduced locally by issuing concurrent requests with retries and observed similar crash pattern.\",\n    \"04:45 UTC - Temporary mitigation applied: added per-tenant gateway rate-limit and low-priority queuing for NoteBase routes; observed reduction in restart frequency.\",\n    \"05:30 UTC - Follow-ups identified: autoscaler cooldown tweak, gateway retry budget enforcement, and an autoserver-side prewarm path for KV cache on failover events. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/3482 for prewarm prototype.\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10 03:25 UTC: Customer reported large fraction of 5xxs after failover. Escalating to SRE \\u2014 tagging @sre-oncall.\",\n    \"Lina Cho (SRE) 2026-03-10 03:33 UTC: Observed high restart rate of serving-runtime in eu-west-1; suspect retry amplification. Temporarily applied per-tenant throttling to NoteBase routes; monitoring impact.\",\n    \"Marco Bell (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-10 04:05 UTC: We can reproduce with a local harness using immediate retries. Opening PR for a conservative prewarm + longer autoscaler warmup: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/3482\",\n    \"Customer (NoteBase SRE) 2026-03-10 04:22 UTC: Thanks \\u2014 we will update our client SDK to add jittered backoff, but we need platform-side mitigations in case of future failovers.\",\n    \"Lina Cho (SRE) 2026-03-10 05:00 UTC: Applied mitigation looks effective \\u2014 5xx rate dropped to baseline after throttling and temporary route fallback to older model variant. Continuing to monitor; will roll platform fixes in next patch window.\",\n    \"Marco Bell (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC: Patch landed to the autoscaler (increase min cooldown to 5m on failover) and gateway now enforces retry budgets per-tenant. Tracking: INT-4130 for staging rollout.\",\n    \"Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12 11:00 UTC: Customer confirmed improved behavior and reduced errors post-fixes. Preparing summary for post-incident review and follow-up action items.\"\n  ],\n  \"resolution\": \"Workaround: applied per-tenant gateway throttling and routed a subset of traffic to an older model variant to reduce memory pressure. Permanent fixes: (1) autoscaler cooldown increase on failover, (2) gateway-level retry budget enforcement, (3) build KV prewarm path triggered on routing shifts. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/3482 contains prewarm prototype; autoscaler change tracked under INT-4130. Customer confirmed resolution on 2026-03-12; ticket will remain open until postmortem published.\",\n  \"postmortem_link\": \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/POSTMORTEM-SUP-87422\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"summary\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"impact\",\n    \"steps_to_reproduce\",\n    \"logs_and_metrics\",\n    \"investigation_notes\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"resolution\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_1e0c6d99da584a5888bfbb38afe2ed60\"\n}",

document.title: Sustained elevated 5xx after regional failover; retry amplification and serving-runtime crashloops
document.content:
{
  "key": "SUP-87422",
  "project": "customer-support",
  "issue_type": "Incident",
  "summary": "Sustained elevated 5xx after regional failover; retry amplification and serving-runtime crashloops",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "severity": "Sev1",
  "created_at": "2026-03-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-12",
  "reporter": "Aisha Patel",
  "assignee": "Marco Bell",
  "customer_company": "NoteBase Inc.",
  "customer_tier": "dedicated",
  "components": [
    "api-gateway",
    "serving-runtime",
    "autoscaler",
    "kvcache",
    "routing"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "5xx",
    "regional-failover",
    "retry-amplification",
    "high-error-rate"
  ],
  "environment": "prod: us-west -> failover -> eu-west",
  "affected_models": [
    "redwood-v1-medium"
  ],
  "affected_regions": [
    "us-west-2",
    "eu-west-1"
  ],
  "sla_due_at": "2026-03-10",
  "first_response_due_at": "2026-03-10",
  "linked_issues": [
    "SUP-62111",
    "SUP-44120"
  ],
  "related_github_prs": [
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/3482"
  ],
  "related_confluence_pages": [
    "https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/FAILOVER-RUNBOOK"
  ],
  "description": "Issue summary: After an automated regional failover on 2026-03-10 at ~03:14 UTC, NoteBase began observing sustained 5xx responses for their production traffic. Impact: customer reports 30-40% of requests returning 5xx (502/503/504) for ~90 minutes and higher latency for the remainder. Environment: NoteBase dedicated tenancy; traffic routed from us-west-2 to eu-west-1 as part of failover policy. Immediate business impact: degraded UX for end users, automated client retries increased request volume.",
  "impact": "Customer-facing production errors; estimated 35% elevated 5xx rate for the customer\u2019s routes; increased cost due to retries and partial throttling by gateway.",
  "steps_to_reproduce": "1) Trigger a regional failover by simulating control-plane evicted nodes scenario in us-west-2 (internal test). 2) Observe routing shift to eu-west-1. 3) Under steady client QPS with exponential backoff disabled, observe a ramp of 5xxs within 5-10 minutes as KV cache warms and runtimes restart. 4) Verify serving-runtime logs showing OOM-ish restarts and high GC/CPU prior to 5xx wave.",
  "logs_and_metrics": "Summarized metrics: gateway 5xx rate jump at 03:14 UTC; serving-runtime process restarts increased 6x; average p95 latency rose from 180ms to 900ms; worker OOM and eviction logs in runtime. Dashboard links: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/ingress/route-NoteBase?from=164&to=204, runtime crash heatmap: https://dash.redwood.ai/runtime/crashmap?range=2h.",
  "investigation_notes": [
    "03:20 UTC - Initial triage: observed routing diverted to eu-west-1; autoscaler initiated scale-up but aggressive scale-down cooldown was still in place causing unstable pool size.",
    "03:35 UTC - Hypothesis: client retries (no jitter) created retry amplification hitting runtimes before KV cache/memory warmed, causing thrash and restarts leading to 5xxs.",
    "03:50 UTC - Evidence: runtime logs show frequent cache misses and high alloc rates; OOM-like terminations preceded many 5xx events. Stack traces attached in linked PR notes.",
    "04:10 UTC - Correlation: customer client library was configured with immediate retries (3 attempts, no backoff). We reproduced locally by issuing concurrent requests with retries and observed similar crash pattern.",
    "04:45 UTC - Temporary mitigation applied: added per-tenant gateway rate-limit and low-priority queuing for NoteBase routes; observed reduction in restart frequency.",
    "05:30 UTC - Follow-ups identified: autoscaler cooldown tweak, gateway retry budget enforcement, and an autoserver-side prewarm path for KV cache on failover events. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/3482 for prewarm prototype."
  ],
  "comments": [
    "Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10 03:25 UTC: Customer reported large fraction of 5xxs after failover. Escalating to SRE \u2014 tagging @sre-oncall.",
    "Lina Cho (SRE) 2026-03-10 03:33 UTC: Observed high restart rate of serving-runtime in eu-west-1; suspect retry amplification. Temporarily applied per-tenant throttling to NoteBase routes; monitoring impact.",
    "Marco Bell (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-10 04:05 UTC: We can reproduce with a local harness using immediate retries. Opening PR for a conservative prewarm + longer autoscaler warmup: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/3482",
    "Customer (NoteBase SRE) 2026-03-10 04:22 UTC: Thanks \u2014 we will update our client SDK to add jittered backoff, but we need platform-side mitigations in case of future failovers.",
    "Lina Cho (SRE) 2026-03-10 05:00 UTC: Applied mitigation looks effective \u2014 5xx rate dropped to baseline after throttling and temporary route fallback to older model variant. Continuing to monitor; will roll platform fixes in next patch window.",
    "Marco Bell (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC: Patch landed to the autoscaler (increase min cooldown to 5m on failover) and gateway now enforces retry budgets per-tenant. Tracking: INT-4130 for staging rollout.",
    "Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12 11:00 UTC: Customer confirmed improved behavior and reduced errors post-fixes. Preparing summary for post-incident review and follow-up action items."
  ],
  "resolution": "Workaround: applied per-tenant gateway throttling and routed a subset of traffic to an older model variant to reduce memory pressure. Permanent fixes: (1) autoscaler cooldown increase on failover, (2) gateway-level retry budget enforcement, (3) build KV prewarm path triggered on routing shifts. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/3482 contains prewarm prototype; autoscaler change tracked under INT-4130. Customer confirmed resolution on 2026-03-12; ticket will remain open until postmortem published.",
  "postmortem_link": "https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/POSTMORTEM-SUP-87422",
  "title_field_name": "summary",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "impact",
    "steps_to_reproduce",
    "logs_and_metrics",
    "investigation_notes",
    "comments",
    "resolution"
  ],

}

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_74d03b5f76ca4372b83e879803b9a573",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/github/perf-canary/pr-427-tighten-p95-regression-thresholds-for-lts.json",
    "title": "Tighten p95 regression thresholds for Runtime LTS gates + document waiver workflow",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/github",
    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"perf-canary\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"427\",\n  \"title\": \"Tighten p95 regression thresholds for Runtime LTS gates + document waiver workflow\",\n  \"author\": \"Jonas Weber\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-19\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-02-24\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2025-02-24\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"release/lts-tighten-p95-thresholds\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Marcus Reed\",\n    \"Claire Dubois\",\n    \"Allison Grant\",\n    \"Connor O'Brien\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"perf\",\n    \"runtime-lts\",\n    \"release-gating\",\n    \"sre\",\n    \"docs\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"ENG-4825\",\n    \"ENG-4821\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_jira\": [\n    \"INT-3368\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"8\",\n  \"additions\": \"214\",\n  \"deletions\": \"63\",\n  \"description\": \"Context: As part of standing up Runtime LTS, we\\u2019re using perf-canary to gate patch releases with a small set of canonical workloads. During the 1.18 LTS pilot we saw a few cases where p95 latency regressed in ways that were operationally meaningful (tail spikes / backpressure) but didn\\u2019t trip the existing thresholds because they were tuned for mainline signal rather than \\u201cslower-change\\u201d LTS expectations.\\n\\nThis PR tightens p95 regression thresholds for the LTS gate and adds explicit documentation for the exception/waiver flow that Release Managers can use when benchmarks are noisy (runner contention, transient GPU clocking variance) or when a known/acceptable tradeoff is made (e.g., deliberate throughput vs tail trade).\\n\\nWhat changed (high level): 1) LTS-specific thresholds: reduce allowed p95 latency regression from 5% -> 3% on the canonical LTS benchmark set; keep p50 at 2% (unchanged) and tighten throughput regression from -4% -> -3% for the same set. 2) Add a minimum sample-count rule for p95 comparisons (avoid false positives on short runs): require >= 20k tokens per scenario before gating is evaluated; otherwise mark as \\u201cinsufficient data\\u201d and require rerun. 3) Add a documented waiver workflow: a single, auditable \\u201cperf-waiver\\u201d artifact linked in the PR / release issue, requiring approvals from Perf Owner + SRE + Release Eng lead, with time-bounded validity (per patch only) and mandatory rerun on dedicated runners if the initial run was on shared capacity.\\n\\nWhy: LTS customers are more sensitive to tail latency regressions because they tend to run closer to reserved capacity and use stricter SLOs; we want the default gate to be conservative. The waiver process is to keep us pragmatic when the measurement system is noisy\\u2014without silently weakening gates.\\n\\nRisk: Tightening gates will increase failures/flake until we reduce runner contention (tracked in INT-3368). This PR mitigates with (a) sample-count rule, (b) rerun guidance, and (c) explicit waiver process rather than ad-hoc \\u201cLGTM, ship it\\u201d decisions.\\n\\nRollout: Enabled only for LTS release-branch workflows (release/* and runtime-*-lts) and leaves main branch thresholds unchanged.\\n\\nTest plan: ran CI unit tests; validated config parsing; dry-ran the LTS workflow against an existing baseline artifact; verified the waiver template renders and is attached to the GitHub Action summary.\\n\\nRefs: ENG-4825 (Integrate perf-canary gates into LTS release), ENG-4821 (Runtime LTS initiative), INT-3368 (benchmark runner capacity).\",\n  \"commits\": [\n    \"perf/gates: add lts profile + tighten p95 thresholds\",\n    \"workflows: apply lts profile only on release/* and *-lts branches\",\n    \"reporting: enforce min sample count for p95 comparisons\",\n    \"docs: add perf gate waiver workflow + required approvals\",\n    \"chore: update baseline schema version + back-compat reader\"\n  ],\n  \"changed_areas\": [\n    \"gates/lts_profile.yaml\",\n    \"gates/default_profile.yaml\",\n    \".github/workflows/bench-release-branch.yml\",\n    \"src/compare/regression_rules.py\",\n    \"src/reporting/action_summary.py\",\n    \"docs/lts/waivers.md\",\n    \"docs/lts/gates.md\",\n    \"tests/test_regression_rules.py\"\n  ],\n  \"notable_snippets\": [\n    \"gates/lts_profile.yaml: p95_latency_regression_max_pct: 3.0 (was 5.0 for LTS gating), throughput_regression_max_pct: -3.0\",\n    \"src/compare/regression_rules.py: require_min_tokens_per_case: 20000; otherwise emit status=INSUFFICIENT_DATA and require rerun\",\n    \"docs/lts/waivers.md: adds waiver template fields (reason, impacted scenarios, rerun links, expiration, approvals)\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_checks\": [\n    \"unit-tests (ubuntu-latest): pass\",\n    \"lint (ruff/flake8): pass\",\n    \"typecheck (mypy): pass\",\n    \"workflow-dryrun (release-branch benchmark config): pass\"\n  ],\n  \"review_conversation\": \"Marcus Reed (Perf test suite owner): The 3% p95 limit feels right for LTS, but we should be explicit about what metric we compare (p95 end-to-end vs model-only). Can you clarify in docs? Also, sample count: is 20k tokens enough for the long-context scenario?\\n\\nJonas Weber (author): Good call. The gate compares end-to-end request latency p95 as emitted by the benchmark harness (includes queueing + runtime). I\\u2019ll add a note in docs/lts/gates.md. Re: 20k tokens\\u2014this is per scenario per variant; for long-context we typically hit ~60\\u2013120k tokens/run, so we should be safe. The rule is mainly preventing short \\u201csmoke\\u201d runs from tripping p95.\\n\\nClaire Dubois (Benchmark methodology): +1 to explicit metric definition. I\\u2019m slightly worried about flake on shared runners with 3%. Can the waiver doc require rerun on dedicated runner capacity before waiver is granted?\\n\\nJonas Weber (author): Yes\\u2014updated waiver doc: if the run was on shared capacity or if the variance indicator > 1.5%, rerun on dedicated runner is mandatory before waiver can be approved.\\n\\nAllison Grant (Observability/perf signals): Waiver workflow needs an audit trail for release managers. Can we make the action upload a waiver form (even if empty) so the release PR has a consistent artifact name?\\n\\nJonas Weber (author): Implemented: the action always publishes a \\u201cperf-waiver.md\\u201d artifact stub. If waiver requested, it must be filled and re-uploaded (or attached in the release PR) with approvals.\\n\\nConnor O'Brien (Release Eng lead): Please align terminology with runtime LTS runbook: \\u201cwaiver\\u201d vs \\u201cexception\\u201d. We\\u2019ve been using \\u201cwaiver\\u201d in runbooks. Also, ensure this only applies to LTS release workflows.\\n\\nJonas Weber (author): Renamed docs and action summary to \\u201cwaiver\\u201d. Confirmed the workflow applies lts_profile only for release/* and *-lts branches. Mainline continues to use default_profile.\\n\\nMarcus Reed: Docs update looks good. One more request: add a reminder that repeated waivers for the same scenario should open an infra ticket (runner contention) or a runtime ticket (real regression). Not a blocker but useful.\\n\\nJonas Weber (author): Added a \\u201cWhen waivers repeat\\u201d section linking to INT-3368 and suggesting filing a runtime perf regression ticket if the same benchmark regresses twice.\\n\\nApprovals: Marcus Reed approved; Claire Dubois approved; Allison Grant approved; Connor O'Brien approved.\",\n  \"merge_outcome\": \"Merged via squash\",\n  \"release_notes\": [\n    \"LTS perf gates now enforce stricter p95 latency and throughput regression thresholds.\",\n    \"Release managers have a documented, auditable waiver workflow for noisy benchmark results.\",\n    \"Added minimum sample-count requirements to reduce false-positive p95 regressions.\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"review_conversation\",\n    \"release_notes\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_74d03b5f76ca4372b83e879803b9a573\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Tighten p95 regression thresholds for Runtime LTS gates + document waiver workflow\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/github\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/github/perf-canary/pr-427-tighten-p95-regression-thresholds-for-lts.json\nConnector: github\nWorkspace: perf-canary\n\nwhy : lts customers are more sensitive to tail latency regressions because they tend to run closer to reserved capacity and use stricter slos ; we want the default gate to be conservative. the waiver process is to keep us pragmatic when the measurement system is noisy — without silently weakening gates. risk : tightening gates will increase failures / flake until we reduce runner contention ( tracked in int - 3368 ). this pr mitigates with ( a ) sample - count rule, ( b ) rerun guidance, and ( c ) explicit waiver process rather than ad - hoc “ lgtm, ship it ” decisions.",

document.title: Tighten p95 regression thresholds for Runtime LTS gates + document waiver workflow
document.content:
{
  "repo": "perf-canary",
  "pr_number": "427",
  "title": "Tighten p95 regression thresholds for Runtime LTS gates + document waiver workflow",
  "author": "Jonas Weber",
  "created_at": "2025-02-19",
  "updated_at": "2025-02-24",
  "merged_at": "2025-02-24",
  "state": "merged",
  "base_branch": "main",
  "head_branch": "release/lts-tighten-p95-thresholds",
  "reviewers": [
    "Marcus Reed",
    "Claire Dubois",
    "Allison Grant",
    "Connor O'Brien"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "perf",
    "runtime-lts",
    "release-gating",
    "sre",
    "docs"
  ],
  "linked_linear": [
    "ENG-4825",
    "ENG-4821"
  ],
  "linked_jira": [
    "INT-3368"
  ],
  "ci_status": "pass",
  "files_changed_count": "8",
  "additions": "214",
  "deletions": "63",
  "description": "Context: As part of standing up Runtime LTS, we\u2019re using perf-canary to gate patch releases with a small set of canonical workloads. During the 1.18 LTS pilot we saw a few cases where p95 latency regressed in ways that were operationally meaningful (tail spikes / backpressure) but didn\u2019t trip the existing thresholds because they were tuned for mainline signal rather than \u201cslower-change\u201d LTS expectations.\n\nThis PR tightens p95 regression thresholds for the LTS gate and adds explicit documentation for the exception/waiver flow that Release Managers can use when benchmarks are noisy (runner contention, transient GPU clocking variance) or when a known/acceptable tradeoff is made (e.g., deliberate throughput vs tail trade).\n\nWhat changed (high level): 1) LTS-specific thresholds: reduce allowed p95 latency regression from 5% -> 3% on the canonical LTS benchmark set; keep p50 at 2% (unchanged) and tighten throughput regression from -4% -> -3% for the same set. 2) Add a minimum sample-count rule for p95 comparisons (avoid false positives on short runs): require >= 20k tokens per scenario before gating is evaluated; otherwise mark as \u201cinsufficient data\u201d and require rerun. 3) Add a documented waiver workflow: a single, auditable \u201cperf-waiver\u201d artifact linked in the PR / release issue, requiring approvals from Perf Owner + SRE + Release Eng lead, with time-bounded validity (per patch only) and mandatory rerun on dedicated runners if the initial run was on shared capacity.\n\nWhy: LTS customers are more sensitive to tail latency regressions because they tend to run closer to reserved capacity and use stricter SLOs; we want the default gate to be conservative. The waiver process is to keep us pragmatic when the measurement system is noisy\u2014without silently weakening gates.\n\nRisk: Tightening gates will increase failures/flake until we reduce runner contention (tracked in INT-3368). This PR mitigates with (a) sample-count rule, (b) rerun guidance, and (c) explicit waiver process rather than ad-hoc \u201cLGTM, ship it\u201d decisions.\n\nRollout: Enabled only for LTS release-branch workflows (release/* and runtime-*-lts) and leaves main branch thresholds unchanged.\n\nTest plan: ran CI unit tests; validated config parsing; dry-ran the LTS workflow against an existing baseline artifact; verified the waiver template renders and is attached to the GitHub Action summary.\n\nRefs: ENG-4825 (Integrate perf-canary gates into LTS release), ENG-4821 (Runtime LTS initiative), INT-3368 (benchmark runner capacity).",
  "commits": [
    "perf/gates: add lts profile + tighten p95 thresholds",
    "workflows: apply lts profile only on release/* and *-lts branches",
    "reporting: enforce min sample count for p95 comparisons",
    "docs: add perf gate waiver workflow + required approvals",
    "chore: update baseline schema version + back-compat reader"
  ],
  "changed_areas": [
    "gates/lts_profile.yaml",
    "gates/default_profile.yaml",
    ".github/workflows/bench-release-branch.yml",
    "src/compare/regression_rules.py",
    "src/reporting/action_summary.py",
    "docs/lts/waivers.md",
    "docs/lts/gates.md",
    "tests/test_regression_rules.py"
  ],
  "notable_snippets": [
    "gates/lts_profile.yaml: p95_latency_regression_max_pct: 3.0 (was 5.0 for LTS gating), throughput_regression_max_pct: -3.0",
    "src/compare/regression_rules.py: require_min_tokens_per_case: 20000; otherwise emit status=INSUFFICIENT_DATA and require rerun",
    "docs/lts/waivers.md: adds waiver template fields (reason, impacted scenarios, rerun links, expiration, approvals)"
  ],
  "ci_checks": [
    "unit-tests (ubuntu-latest): pass",
    "lint (ruff/flake8): pass",
    "typecheck (mypy): pass",
    "workflow-dryrun (release-branch benchmark config): pass"
  ],
  "review_conversation": "Marcus Reed (Perf test suite owner): The 3% p95 limit feels right for LTS, but we should be explicit about what metric we compare (p95 end-to-end vs model-only). Can you clarify in docs? Also, sample count: is 20k tokens enough for the long-context scenario?\n\nJonas Weber (author): Good call. The gate compares end-to-end request latency p95 as emitted by the benchmark harness (includes queueing + runtime). I\u2019ll add a note in docs/lts/gates.md. Re: 20k tokens\u2014this is per scenario per variant; for long-context we typically hit ~60\u2013120k tokens/run, so we should be safe. The rule is mainly preventing short \u201csmoke\u201d runs from tripping p95.\n\nClaire Dubois (Benchmark methodology): +1 to explicit metric definition. I\u2019m slightly worried about flake on shared runners with 3%. Can the waiver doc require rerun on dedicated runner capacity before waiver is granted?\n\nJonas Weber (author): Yes\u2014updated waiver doc: if the run was on shared capacity or if the variance indicator > 1.5%, rerun on dedicated runner is mandatory before waiver can be approved.\n\nAllison Grant (Observability/perf signals): Waiver workflow needs an audit trail for release managers. Can we make the action upload a waiver form (even if empty) so the release PR has a consistent artifact name?\n\nJonas Weber (author): Implemented: the action always publishes a \u201cperf-waiver.md\u201d artifact stub. If waiver requested, it must be filled and re-uploaded (or attached in the release PR) with approvals.\n\nConnor O'Brien (Release Eng lead): Please align terminology with runtime LTS runbook: \u201cwaiver\u201d vs \u201cexception\u201d. We\u2019ve been using \u201cwaiver\u201d in runbooks. Also, ensure this only applies to LTS release workflows.\n\nJonas Weber (author): Renamed docs and action summary to \u201cwaiver\u201d. Confirmed the workflow applies lts_profile only for release/* and *-lts branches. Mainline continues to use default_profile.\n\nMarcus Reed: Docs update looks good. One more request: add a reminder that repeated waivers for the same scenario should open an infra ticket (runner contention) or a runtime ticket (real regression). Not a blocker but useful.\n\nJonas Weber (author): Added a \u201cWhen waivers repeat\u201d section linking to INT-3368 and suggesting filing a runtime perf regression ticket if the same benchmark regresses twice.\n\nApprovals: Marcus Reed approved; Claire Dubois approved; Allison Grant approved; Connor O'Brien approved.",
  "merge_outcome": "Merged via squash",
  "release_notes": [
    "LTS perf gates now enforce stricter p95 latency and throughput regression thresholds.",
    "Release managers have a documented, auditable waiver workflow for noisy benchmark results.",
    "Added minimum sample-count requirements to reduce false-positive p95 regressions."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "review_conversation",
    "release_notes"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_74d03b5f76ca4372b83e879803b9a573"
}

    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Operational Flows and Policy Gallery\",\n  \"space\": \"policies-and-process\",\n  \"author\": \"Maya Chen\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"finance-legal\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-08-01\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Diego Alvarez\",\n    \"Samira Patel\",\n    \"Ethan Ross\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"access-control\",\n    \"change-management\",\n    \"procurement\",\n    \"vendor-management\",\n    \"travel\",\n    \"templates\",\n    \"data-management\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/policies-and-process/central-policy-index-and-core-processes-2025.json\",\n    \"/confluence/policies-and-process/operational-compendium-2026.json\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"body\": \"Purpose and scope:\\n\\nThis page consolidates company-wide operational flows and reusable policy artifacts relating to access and permissions, change management, data lifecycle, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel policy, and internal templates. It is intended as a single-entry reference for teams to discover the canonical process, required approvals, and the standard templates used by Redwood Inference.\\n\\nAudience:\\n- Engineering, Product, Security, Finance, People Ops, and Procurement partners.\\n- Team leads and managers who approve access, spend, or changes.\\n\\nSummary (quick reference):\\n| Area | Owner | Target SLA / Thresholds | Key system | Approval path |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| Access & Permissions | Security + IT | Standard request: 48 hours; Elevated: 5 business days; Emergency: <4 hours | IdentityHub (IAM) | Manager -> Security reviewer -> IAM admin |\\n| Change Management | Eng-Platform | Standard change window: 02:00\\u201305:00 PST; Emergency changes: immediate runbook | OpsChange | Change owner -> CAB -> Release manager |\\n| Data Management | Security + Data Platform | Retention: 1y/3y/7y by classification; Backup RPO 24h | DataLake / Vault | Data owner -> Security review |\\n| Procurement & Expenses | Finance-Legal | < $5k: manager; $5k\\u2013$75k: procurement; > $75k: exec | ProcureFlow, Spendly | Req -> Procurement -> Finance -> Exec (if needed) |\\n| Vendor Management | Procurement | Onboarding: 7\\u201314 days | Vendor Portal | Security review -> Procurement -> Contracting |\\n| Travel & Expenses | People Ops + Finance | Per-diem and policy; pre-approval for > $2k | Spendly | Traveler -> Manager -> Finance |\\n\\nNote: See \\\"Templates\\\" section at the end for direct links to request and approval forms.\\n\\n1) Access & Permissions (Identity lifecycle)\\n\\nOverview:\\nRedwood centralizes identity and access control to IdentityHub. All access must follow least-privilege principles and be tied to an owner and business justification. Temporary elevated access must have an expiration.\\n\\nRoles and responsibilities:\\n- Requester: submits request in IdentityHub with justification and business owner.\\n- Manager: approves role change and validates business need.\\n- Security reviewer: performs risk review for privileged access (SRE/infra, customer data, KMS/HSM).\\n- IAM admin: applies the change and documents in the audit log.\\n\\nStandard process (step-by-step):\\n1. Requester files an Access Request in IdentityHub with resource, role, justification, and requested duration.\\n2. Manager approves or rejects within 48 hours. If no response, escalate to manager's skip-level.\\n3. If the role is privileged, Security reviewer has 2 business days to respond; may place conditions (MFA, limited scope).\\n4. IAM admin provisions access. Provisioning events must include ticket ID and expiration.\\n\\nSLOs and monitoring:\\n- 90% of standard requests fulfilled within 48 hours.\\n- Emergency access (investigations, P1 incidents): target same-day (4 hours) turnaround via on-call IAM admin and Security Pager.\\n- Monthly audit: all privileged roles reviewed quarterly.\\n\\nExceptions and emergency process:\\n- Emergency access uses the Emergency Access Runbook (link: OpsChange/Emergency-Access-Runbook). Every emergency grant must be accompanied by an audit ticket and post-incident access review within 7 days.\\n\\n2) Change Management (Services & Infra)\\n\\nPurpose:\\nTo minimize risk from configuration and code changes by standardizing assessment, scheduling, and rollouts.\\n\\nChange categories:\\n- Standard changes: pre-approved, low-risk, follow templated rollout (e.g., dependency bumps, non-prod config changes).\\n- Normal changes: require CAB review; typically feature deploys, infra patches.\\n- Emergency changes: require immediate action; follow Emergency Change runbook and postmortem.\\n\\nApproval matrix and windows:\\n- Standard changes: no CAB if they match the Standard Change Catalogue and use a validated automation playbook.\\n- Normal changes: submit in OpsChange 72 hours before planned window. CAB meets daily for fast lanes and weekly for large changes.\\n- Change window: default maintenance window 02:00\\u201305:00 PST; services with global usage must consult SRE before scheduling.\\n\\nRollback policy:\\n- All normal and emergency changes must include a rollback plan and a success metric (SLO delta or error rate).\\n- If errors exceed alert threshold (error rate > 0.5% or latency > 2x baseline), trigger rollback and incident response.\\n\\nPost-change verification:\\n- Owner must run the Post-Change Checklist in OpsChange within 4 hours of completion and mark the change as successful or failed.\\n\\n3) Data Management (Classification, Retention, Access)\\n\\nClassification table:\\n| Classification | Examples | Default retention | Access controls |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| Public | Marketing assets | 0 | Read-only public URLs |\\n| Internal | Documentation, non-sensitive logs | 3 years | Corporate SSO with RBAC |\\n| Confidential | Customer PII, analytics with identifiers | 7 years | Justified access, strict logging, DLP |\\n| Restricted | KMS keys, secrets, regulated customer data | As required by contract | Restricted to named individuals, HSM/KMS controls |\\n\\nData handling requirements:\\n- PII and Confidential datasets require a documented Data Processing Agreement and must be stored only in Vault-backed buckets with encryption at rest.\\n- Backups: daily snapshot with retention according to classification. Restore drills: annually for Restricted data, bi-annually for Confidential.\\n\\nRetention and deletion:\\n- Automated retention policies are enforced via DataLife jobs. Data owners must declare retention period at onboarding.\\n- Deletion requests use the Data Deletion Template and are tracked in the Data Deletion Register.\\n\\nData change control:\\n- Schema migrations that touch production must be submitted to Data Platform and follow the Migration Review workflow (submit migration PR, canary run, monitoring).\\n\\n4) Procurement & Expenses\\n\\nProcurement thresholds and approvals:\\n- <$5,000: Manager approval via ProcureFlow (Spendly card optional).\\n- $5,000\\u2013$75,000: Procurement team approval + Finance-Legal review (Supplier terms assessment).\\n- >$75,000: Procurement + Finance-Legal + Executive approval (SVP or CFO).\\n- Capital spend: follow Capitalization policy; enter requisition with finance tag.\\n\\nCompetitive sourcing and vendor evaluation:\\n- For purchases > $50k, obtain at least 2 competitive quotes and document selection rationale in ProcureFlow.\\n- Risk scoring: Procurement assigns a Vendor Risk Score (1\\u201310). Any vendor with score >=7 triggers Security review and may require SOC2/ISO evidence.\\n\\nExpense reimbursement rules (high level):\\n- Use Spendly to submit expense reports. Receipts required for all items > $25.\\n- Per-diem for domestic travel: $75/day lodging cap: $250/night without pre-approval.\\n- International travel: pre-approval required for trips exceeding $2,000.\\n\\nAudit and controls:\\n- Monthly reconciliation between ProcureFlow and accounting.\\n- Random sample expense audits quarterly (finance + internal audit).\\n\\n5) Vendor Management\\n\\nOnboarding checklist (7\\u201314 day target):\\n1. Vendor request created in Vendor Portal (ProcureFlow) with SOW/quote.\\n2. Procurement performs commercial review and risk scoring.\\n3. Security runs technical and compliance review (SOC2/penetration test evidence as required).\\n4. Legal reviews contract terms and data processing clauses.\\n5. Finance provisions payment terms and payment method.\\n6. Account team verifies go/no-go.\\n\\nContractual controls and SLAs:\\n- Standard contract must include: data residency clause, breach notification timeline (<=72 hours), liability caps, and SLA definitions (uptime, support response).\\n- For production services that affect customer traffic, require 99.9% uptime SLA and a runbook integration.\\n\\nOffboarding and termination:\\n- On contract end, Procurement triggers Offboarding Checklist: license termination, access revocation in IdentityHub, data return or secure deletion, final invoice settlement.\\n\\n6) Travel policy (concise)\\n\\nPre-approval:\\n- Any trip expected to exceed $2,000 requires manager & finance pre-approval via Spendly.\\n\\nTravel safety and insurance:\\n- All employees traveling on business automatically receive Redwood travel insurance and are covered under the company incident response procedures.\\n\\nBooking and allowable expenses:\\n- Use company preferred vendors where available. Personal upgrades should not be charged to company cards without explicit manager approval.\\n\\nExpense timelines:\\n- Submit expense reports within 10 business days of trip completion. Late submissions may delay reimbursement.\\n\\n7) Templates and artifacts (canonical)\\n\\nAvailable templates (ProcureFlow / Confluence Templates):\\n- Access Request Template (IdentityHub Request Form) -> /confluence/templates/access-request-template\\n- Change Request Template (OpsChange Change Form) -> /confluence/templates/change-request-template\\n- Data Deletion Request -> /confluence/templates/data-deletion-request\\n- Vendor Onboarding Checklist -> /confluence/templates/vendor-onboarding-checklist\\n- Low-value Purchase Requisition (<$5k) -> /confluence/templates/requisition-lowvalue\\n- Expense Report Template (Spendly) -> /confluence/templates/expense-report-template\\n\\nExample JSON/YAML snippets:\\n- Minimal change request example (YAML):\\n---\\ntitle: \\\"Upgrade dependency X\\\"\\ncomponents: [service-a, service-b]\\nwindow: \\\"2026-09-01T02:00:00-07:00 to 2026-09-01T05:00:00-07:00\\\"\\nrollback: \\\"helm rollback v1\\\"\\nowner: \\\"team-service-owner@example.com\\\"\\n---\\n\\nAudit and enforcement:\\n- Policy exceptions must be recorded using the Exception Request Template and approved by the policy owner. Exceptions are logged and reviewed quarterly.\\n- Non-compliance (unapproved access, unauthorized spend) escalates to the owner_team and may be subject to disciplinary action per HR policy.\\n\\nOperational readiness and playbooks:\\n- Each area above has an associated runbook stored in OpsChange and linked from this page. Runbooks include command snippets, contact on-call rotation, and verification checks.\\n\\nChange log for this page:\\n- 2026-02-10: Created by Maya Chen (initial gallery and templates).\\n- 2026-05-12: Procurement thresholds updated; added vendor risk scoring (Diego Alvarez).\\n- 2026-08-01: Added emergency access SLA details and retention clarifications (Samira Patel).\\n\\nContact and ownership:\\n- Primary owner: Finance-Legal (policy lead: Maya Chen, maya.chen@redwood.com).\\n- For operational questions: security@redwood.com, procurement@redwood.com, people-ops@redwood.com.\\n\\nRelated resources and links:\\n- Central Policy Index: /confluence/policies-and-process/central-policy-index-and-core-processes-2025.json\\n- OpsChange runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/\\n- IdentityHub operator docs: /confluence/eng-infra/iam/\\n\\nHow to request updates to this gallery:\\n- Submit a PR against this page via the internal docs workflow or email the policy lead. All updates must list reviewers and a summary of change.\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_36d7605113204cdca94405cb30fc2c10\"\n}",

document.title: Operational Flows and Policy Gallery
document.content:
{
  "title": "Operational Flows and Policy Gallery",
  "space": "policies-and-process",
  "author": "Maya Chen",
  "owner_team": "finance-legal",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-10",
  "last_updated": "2026-08-01",
  "reviewers": [
    "Diego Alvarez",
    "Samira Patel",
    "Ethan Ross"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "access-control",
    "change-management",
    "procurement",
    "vendor-management",
    "travel",
    "templates",
    "data-management"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/policies-and-process/central-policy-index-and-core-processes-2025.json",
    "/confluence/policies-and-process/operational-compendium-2026.json"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "Purpose and scope:

This page consolidates company-wide operational flows and reusable policy artifacts relating to access and permissions, change management, data lifecycle, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel policy, and internal templates. It is intended as a single-entry reference for teams to discover the canonical process, required approvals, and the standard templates used by Redwood Inference.

Audience:
- Engineering, Product, Security, Finance, People Ops, and Procurement partners.
- Team leads and managers who approve access, spend, or changes.

Summary (quick reference):
| Area | Owner | Target SLA / Thresholds | Key system | Approval path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Access & Permissions | Security + IT | Standard request: 48 hours; Elevated: 5 business days; Emergency: <4 hours | IdentityHub (IAM) | Manager -> Security reviewer -> IAM admin |
| Change Management | Eng-Platform | Standard change window: 02:00–05:00 PST; Emergency changes: immediate runbook | OpsChange | Change owner -> CAB -> Release manager |
| Data Management | Security + Data Platform | Retention: 1y/3y/7y by classification; Backup RPO 24h | DataLake / Vault | Data owner -> Security review |
| Procurement & Expenses | Finance-Legal | < $5k: manager; $5k–$75k: procurement; > $75k: exec | ProcureFlow, Spendly | Req -> Procurement -> Finance -> Exec (if needed) |
| Vendor Management | Procurement | Onboarding: 7–14 days | Vendor Portal | Security review -> Procurement -> Contracting |
| Travel & Expenses | People Ops + Finance | Per-diem and policy; pre-approval for > $2k | Spendly | Traveler -> Manager -> Finance |

Note: See "Templates" section at the end for direct links to request and approval forms.

1) Access & Permissions (Identity lifecycle)

Overview:
Redwood centralizes identity and access control to IdentityHub. All access must follow least-privilege principles and be tied to an owner and business justification. Temporary elevated access must have an expiration.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Requester: submits request in IdentityHub with justification and business owner.
- Manager: approves role change and validates business need.
- Security reviewer: performs risk review for privileged access (SRE/infra, customer data, KMS/HSM).
- IAM admin: applies the change and documents in the audit log.

Standard process (step-by-step):
1. Requester files an Access Request in IdentityHub with resource, role, justification, and requested duration.
2. Manager approves or rejects within 48 hours. If no response, escalate to manager's skip-level.
3. If the role is privileged, Security reviewer has 2 business days to respond; may place conditions (MFA, limited scope).
4. IAM admin provisions access. Provisioning events must include ticket ID and expiration.

SLOs and monitoring:
- 90% of standard requests fulfilled within 48 hours.
- Emergency access (investigations, P1 incidents): target same-day (4 hours) turnaround via on-call IAM admin and Security Pager.
- Monthly audit: all privileged roles reviewed quarterly.

Exceptions and emergency process:
- Emergency access uses the Emergency Access Runbook (link: OpsChange/Emergency-Access-Runbook). Every emergency grant must be accompanied by an audit ticket and post-incident access review within 7 days.

2) Change Management (Services & Infra)

Purpose:
To minimize risk from configuration and code changes by standardizing assessment, scheduling, and rollouts.

Change categories:
- Standard changes: pre-approved, low-risk, follow templated rollout (e.g., dependency bumps, non-prod config changes).
- Normal changes: require CAB review; typically feature deploys, infra patches.
- Emergency changes: require immediate action; follow Emergency Change runbook and postmortem.

Approval matrix and windows:
- Standard changes: no CAB if they match the Standard Change Catalogue and use a validated automation playbook.
- Normal changes: submit in OpsChange 72 hours before planned window. CAB meets daily for fast lanes and weekly for large changes.
- Change window: default maintenance window 02:00–05:00 PST; services with global usage must consult SRE before scheduling.

Rollback policy:
- All normal and emergency changes must include a rollback plan and a success metric (SLO delta or error rate).
- If errors exceed alert threshold (error rate > 0.5% or latency > 2x baseline), trigger rollback and incident response.

Post-change verification:
- Owner must run the Post-Change Checklist in OpsChange within 4 hours of completion and mark the change as successful or failed.

3) Data Management (Classification, Retention, Access)

Classification table:
| Classification | Examples | Default retention | Access controls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public | Marketing assets | 0 | Read-only public URLs |
| Internal | Documentation, non-sensitive logs | 3 years | Corporate SSO with RBAC |
| Confidential | Customer PII, analytics with identifiers | 7 years | Justified access, strict logging, DLP |
| Restricted | KMS keys, secrets, regulated customer data | As required by contract | Restricted to named individuals, HSM/KMS controls |

Data handling requirements:
- PII and Confidential datasets require a documented Data Processing Agreement and must be stored only in Vault-backed buckets with encryption at rest.
- Backups: daily snapshot with retention according to classification. Restore drills: annually for Restricted data, bi-annually for Confidential.

Retention and deletion:
- Automated retention policies are enforced via DataLife jobs. Data owners must declare retention period at onboarding.
- Deletion requests use the Data Deletion Template and are tracked in the Data Deletion Register.

Data change control:
- Schema migrations that touch production must be submitted to Data Platform and follow the Migration Review workflow (submit migration PR, canary run, monitoring).

4) Procurement & Expenses

Procurement thresholds and approvals:
- <$5,000: Manager approval via ProcureFlow (Spendly card optional).
- $5,000–$75,000: Procurement team approval + Finance-Legal review (Supplier terms assessment).
- >$75,000: Procurement + Finance-Legal + Executive approval (SVP or CFO).
- Capital spend: follow Capitalization policy; enter requisition with finance tag.

Competitive sourcing and vendor evaluation:
- For purchases > $50k, obtain at least 2 competitive quotes and document selection rationale in ProcureFlow.
- Risk scoring: Procurement assigns a Vendor Risk Score (1–10). Any vendor with score >=7 triggers Security review and may require SOC2/ISO evidence.

Expense reimbursement rules (high level):
- Use Spendly to submit expense reports. Receipts required for all items > $25.
- Per-diem for domestic travel: $75/day lodging cap: $250/night without pre-approval.
- International travel: pre-approval required for trips exceeding $2,000.

Audit and controls:
- Monthly reconciliation between ProcureFlow and accounting.
- Random sample expense audits quarterly (finance + internal audit).

5) Vendor Management

Onboarding checklist (7–14 day target):
1. Vendor request created in Vendor Portal (ProcureFlow) with SOW/quote.
2. Procurement performs commercial review and risk scoring.
3. Security runs technical and compliance review (SOC2/penetration test evidence as required).
4. Legal reviews contract terms and data processing clauses.
5. Finance provisions payment terms and payment method.
6. Account team verifies go/no-go.

Contractual controls and SLAs:
- Standard contract must include: data residency clause, breach notification timeline (<=72 hours), liability caps, and SLA definitions (uptime, support response).
- For production services that affect customer traffic, require 99.9% uptime SLA and a runbook integration.

Offboarding and termination:
- On contract end, Procurement triggers Offboarding Checklist: license termination, access revocation in IdentityHub, data return or secure deletion, final invoice settlement.

6) Travel policy (concise)

Pre-approval:
- Any trip expected to exceed $2,000 requires manager & finance pre-approval via Spendly.

Travel safety and insurance:
- All employees traveling on business automatically receive Redwood travel insurance and are covered under the company incident response procedures.

Booking and allowable expenses:
- Use company preferred vendors where available. Personal upgrades should not be charged to company cards without explicit manager approval.

Expense timelines:
- Submit expense reports within 10 business days of trip completion. Late submissions may delay reimbursement.

7) Templates and artifacts (canonical)

Available templates (ProcureFlow / Confluence Templates):
- Access Request Template (IdentityHub Request Form) -> /confluence/templates/access-request-template
- Change Request Template (OpsChange Change Form) -> /confluence/templates/change-request-template
- Data Deletion Request -> /confluence/templates/data-deletion-request
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist -> /confluence/templates/vendor-onboarding-checklist
- Low-value Purchase Requisition (<$5k) -> /confluence/templates/requisition-lowvalue
- Expense Report Template (Spendly) -> /confluence/templates/expense-report-template

Example JSON/YAML snippets:
- Minimal change request example (YAML):
---
title: "Upgrade dependency X"
components: [service-a, service-b]
window: "2026-09-01T02:00:00-07:00 to 2026-09-01T05:00:00-07:00"
rollback: "helm rollback v1"
owner: "team-service-owner@example.com"
---

Audit and enforcement:
- Policy exceptions must be recorded using the Exception Request Template and approved by the policy owner. Exceptions are logged and reviewed quarterly.
- Non-compliance (unapproved access, unauthorized spend) escalates to the owner_team and may be subject to disciplinary action per HR policy.

Operational readiness and playbooks:
- Each area above has an associated runbook stored in OpsChange and linked from this page. Runbooks include command snippets, contact on-call rotation, and verification checks.

Change log for this page:
- 2026-02-10: Created by Maya Chen (initial gallery and templates).
- 2026-05-12: Procurement thresholds updated; added vendor risk scoring (Diego Alvarez).
- 2026-08-01: Added emergency access SLA details and retention clarifications (Samira Patel).

Contact and ownership:
- Primary owner: Finance-Legal (policy lead: Maya Chen, maya.chen@redwood.com).
- For operational questions: security@redwood.com, procurement@redwood.com, people-ops@redwood.com.

Related resources and links:
- Central Policy Index: /confluence/policies-and-process/central-policy-index-and-core-processes-2025.json
- OpsChange runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/
- IdentityHub operator docs: /confluence/eng-infra/iam/

How to request updates to this gallery:
- Submit a PR against this page via the internal docs workflow or email the policy lead. All updates must list reviewers and a summary of change.

  "content_field_names": [
    "body"
  ],

}

    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"incidents\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"1780456789\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"1780456789\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"1780460200\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"arun\",\n    \"lina\",\n    \"sam\",\n    \"maria\",\n    \"elliot\",\n    \"ops-bot\",\n    \"support-bot\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": \"arun: Quick sync on INC-4321 postmortem follow-ups. Need a concise playbook for external comms + clear owners for remediation tracking. Main things: status page text, customer-facing summary template, who gets full RCA and when, and an explicit owner for each action item. Can we lock this now?\\n\\nlina: I can author the status page blurb and a short FAQ entry for the public post. Will keep it <3 lines and link to the PM. Planning to publish within 90 minutes after sign-off.\\n\\nsam: i'll take the customer-facing summaries for impacted accounts. Plan: two tiers: (A) all impacted customers get a 1-paragraph summary same day; (B) enterprise/regulatory customers get an expanded report after review. I need the impacted list from support.\\n\\nsupport-bot: SUP-1156 created to collect impacted accounts for INC-4321. Assigned to @elliot. Please update with account IDs and contact emails by EOD.\\n\\nelliot: on it. will have a preliminary list in the ticket in 2 hours. If customers opted out of incident emails previously, i'll flag that.\\n\\nmaria: legal/contract note: any document that includes internal mitigation steps or non-public timelines must be gated and reviewed. We can provide a redacted public summary immediately, but for full RCA distribution allow 72 hours for legal review for regulated accounts.\\n\\narun: thanks. Proposed policy: public status page + short summary (owner: lina) within 2 hours; targeted customer email (owner: sam/support) within same business day; full RCA to customers with NDA/regulatory need (owner: maria) within 72h after review. Also link every action item to our Action Tracker/JIRA. Agree?\\n\\nlina: agree. Draft status blurb I'll post in a minute: ```Status: Reduced API availability, ~45m window on 2026-03-23 UTC. Impact: increased latency and intermittent errors. Mitigation applied; permanent fix in progress. Postmortem: https://redwood.example.com/postmortems/INC-4321```\\n\\nsam: good. For the customer email template i'll use bullets: outage window, observable impact, what we did immediately, ETA for fix, next steps, who to contact. Keep root cause phrasing non-sensitive: \\\"engineering regression related to retry/backoff handling.\\\"\\n\\nmaria: add line: \\\"If you require an audited technical report for compliance, reply and we'll coordinate a reviewed copy.\\\" That avoids accidental over-sharing.\\n\\narun: jess (not here) listed remediation tasks in the PM. We need concrete owners/timestamps in Action Tracker. Who will own implementation and verification?\\n\\njess: (joins) i'll own remediation delivery. Actions I see: revert bad change + confirm metrics (48h), canary rollout + alerting (72h), CI regression test (7 days). I'll put JIRA PM-789 items and link to the PM.\\n\\nelliot: i'll add an \\\"incident recurrence\\\" note in the PM citing the Jan regression pattern, and add recommended customer-facing language for sales/support.\\n\\narun: good. Two operational asks: 1) support to tag enterprise accounts so custops can route the detailed reports, 2) ops to capture deploy/rollback logs we can attach to full RCAs.\\n\\nsupport-bot: SUP-1156 updated with tags; please review.\\n\\nops-bot: Deploy job depl-982 started for rollback. Command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-service --to-revision=203`. Logs streaming -> /var/log/deploys/depl-982.log\\n\\nsam: hold on customer emails until ops-bot confirms rollback success, otherwise customers will get conflicting messages.\\n\\njess: rollback succeeded. I'll post verification metrics in PM and update PM-789.\\n\\nlina: posting status page update now with the approved blurb.\\n\\narun: final reminder: capture everything in the Action Tracker with owners + ETA, and set a recurring review in 2 weeks to check for regressions. Also adding a note to Sales playbook with suggested phrasing about recurrence risk and mitigation roadmap.\\n\\nmaria: i'll review any expanded reports before they go out. Ping me on the SUP ticket when ready.\\n\\narun: thanks everyone. i'll close this thread once all Action Tracker items have owners and SUP-1156 is populated. Reopen here if blockers. :thumbsup:\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_27ef80109fea4f64878c5c239b7874c7\"\n}",

{
  "channel": "incidents",
  "thread_ts": "1780456789",
  "first_message_ts": "1780456789",
  "last_message_ts": "1780460200",
  "participants": [
    "arun",
    "lina",
    "sam",
    "maria",
    "elliot",
    "ops-bot",
    "support-bot"
  ],
  "messages": "arun: Quick sync on INC-4321 postmortem follow-ups. Need a concise playbook for external comms + clear owners for remediation tracking. Main things: status page text, customer-facing summary template, who gets full RCA and when, and an explicit owner for each action item. Can we lock this now?

lina: I can author the status page blurb and a short FAQ entry for the public post. Will keep it <3 lines and link to the PM. Planning to publish within 90 minutes after sign-off.

sam: i'll take the customer-facing summaries for impacted accounts. Plan: two tiers: (A) all impacted customers get a 1-paragraph summary same day; (B) enterprise/regulatory customers get an expanded report after review. I need the impacted list from support.

support-bot: SUP-1156 created to collect impacted accounts for INC-4321. Assigned to @elliot. Please update with account IDs and contact emails by EOD.

elliot: on it. will have a preliminary list in the ticket in 2 hours. If customers opted out of incident emails previously, i'll flag that.

maria: legal/contract note: any document that includes internal mitigation steps or non-public timelines must be gated and reviewed. We can provide a redacted public summary immediately, but for full RCA distribution allow 72 hours for legal review for regulated accounts.

arun: thanks. Proposed policy: public status page + short summary (owner: lina) within 2 hours; targeted customer email (owner: sam/support) within same business day; full RCA to customers with NDA/regulatory need (owner: maria) within 72h after review. Also link every action item to our Action Tracker/JIRA. Agree?

lina: agree. Draft status blurb I'll post in a minute: ```Status: Reduced API availability, ~45m window on 2026-03-23 UTC. Impact: increased latency and intermittent errors. Mitigation applied; permanent fix in progress. Postmortem: https://redwood.example.com/postmortems/INC-4321```

sam: good. For the customer email template i'll use bullets: outage window, observable impact, what we did immediately, ETA for fix, next steps, who to contact. Keep root cause phrasing non-sensitive: "engineering regression related to retry/backoff handling."

maria: add line: "If you require an audited technical report for compliance, reply and we'll coordinate a reviewed copy." That avoids accidental over-sharing.

arun: jess (not here) listed remediation tasks in the PM. We need concrete owners/timestamps in Action Tracker. Who will own implementation and verification?

jess: (joins) i'll own remediation delivery. Actions I see: revert bad change + confirm metrics (48h), canary rollout + alerting (72h), CI regression test (7 days). I'll put JIRA PM-789 items and link to the PM.

elliot: i'll add an "incident recurrence" note in the PM citing the Jan regression pattern, and add recommended customer-facing language for sales/support.

arun: good. Two operational asks: 1) support to tag enterprise accounts so custops can route the detailed reports, 2) ops to capture deploy/rollback logs we can attach to full RCAs.

support-bot: SUP-1156 updated with tags; please review.

ops-bot: Deploy job depl-982 started for rollback. Command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-service --to-revision=203`. Logs streaming -> /var/log/deploys/depl-982.log

sam: hold on customer emails until ops-bot confirms rollback success, otherwise customers will get conflicting messages.

jess: rollback succeeded. I'll post verification metrics in PM and update PM-789.

lina: posting status page update now with the approved blurb.

arun: final reminder: capture everything in the Action Tracker with owners + ETA, and set a recurring review in 2 weeks to check for regressions. Also adding a note to Sales playbook with suggested phrasing about recurrence risk and mitigation roadmap.

maria: i'll review any expanded reports before they go out. Ping me on the SUP ticket when ready.

arun: thanks everyone. i'll close this thread once all Action Tracker items have owners and SUP-1156 is populated. Reopen here if blockers. :thumbsup:",

arguments.title: Runtime investigation validation and promotion procedure
arguments.summary: For Runtime Diagnostics work: preserve immutable incident/change identifiers; reproduce or bound the customer/SLO symptom; test runtime, scheduling, capacity/quota, cache, routing, and retry hypotheses; name the primary owner; validate under SRE-controlled canary checkpoints; compare original error/latency signals; preserve deploy and rollback logs; require code-owner review, SRE approval, regression coverage or approved exception, and a 14-day recurrence review before promotion. Regional failover and release acceptance thresholds are governed by the final Runtime Diagnostics charter.
